changelog.sentence: Records v1 publishes the rules any tool follows to keep a project's work on GitHub, with a kit that reports each record breaking them.

Anyone can plug a place that runs agents into OpenWiz with a small driver: `kernel/driver.v1.md` defines its four commands, `adapters/template/` is a minimal one to copy, and a five-check test kit shows whether a driver passes.

The installer copies OpenWiz skills into the agents you already use (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and Grok) and leaves your own skills and missing agents untouched; checked on synthetic home folders only.
The `send`, `new` and `attachment` commands, the local web view and its server and service are gone; the app now lives at openwiz.dev/app.
An install made before the server, service and web files were removed now passes `install status` and can update to a newer package.
`openwiz init` now reports a label as set up only when GitHub shows it, and stops before proposing the brain when a label could not be made; checked on a synthetic GitHub only.
The driver test kit now catches every credential format the status contract lists, and never copies a driver answer that holds a credential into its own output.
The skills install no longer deletes a folder or file of yours at its staging or backup path, and refuses before copying anything; checked on synthetic home folders only.

The template driver now stops every process a run's turns started, starts no second agent when woken during a running turn or by two wakes at once, and starts nothing it cannot save (checked on synthetic harnesses).
A project chooses where its agents run with one `Host:` line in `docs/agents/host.md`, and changing that line moves later starts to the new host.
A project chooses where its builders run with one `Host:` line in `docs/agents/host.md`, and changing that line moves later builder starts to the new host; reviewers still start as before.

On synthetic harnesses, the template driver stops every process a supervised run's turns started, starts no second agent when woken during a running turn or by two wakes at once, launches nothing when its pre-launch save fails, and reports an unknown outcome when a turn's final save fails.
A boat.dev driver starts, wakes and stops builders in boat.dev cloud sandboxes through your own signed-in `boat` CLI.
The Cloudroom driver in `adapters/cloudroom/` starts, wakes and stops builders as Cloudroom threads through your own signed-in `room-cli`, and passes the driver kit on a synthetic `room-cli`.
OpenWiz can run builders on the computer or VPS you are on, several at once, with the `claude` or `codex` you already signed into, through the local driver in `adapters/local/`.
The 0.1.0 GitHub release is named OpenWiz 0.01; its tag and changelog heading stay 0.1.0.
OpenWiz installs WizSkills 0.2.0: 18 shorter skills, with onboarding folded into `install` and plan-graph split into `to-spec` and `to-tickets`.
On synthetic fixtures, the boat.dev driver wakes a run whose turn has ended when `boat info` nests the sandbox state, and still refuses a stopped sandbox.
The release package carries the boat.dev, Cloudroom and local host drivers and the driver test kit, under the installed `runtime/adapters/` and `runtime/kernel/`.
`install skills` no longer refuses every harness when `~/.config` is a link and OpenCode is not set up; a harness that is set up behind a linked folder is refused with the folder to fix.

published_changelog: Sign in with GitHub at openwiz.dev/app to see what needs you, every spec's live ticket graph and the agents at work, on a laptop or a phone.

Choose where your builders run, from Linux or macOS, with one `Host:` line in `docs/agents/host.md`: the computer or VPS you are on, with the `claude` or `codex` you already signed into, Cloudroom threads, or boat.dev cloud sandboxes.
Installing puts OpenWiz's skills into the agents you already use (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and Grok) and leaves your own skills untouched; they are now WizSkills 0.2.1, 18 shorter skills.
The `send`, `new` and `attachment` commands, the local web view and its server and service are gone: OpenWiz is now the command, the drivers and the skills, and the app lives on the web.

Anyone can plug a place that runs agents into OpenWiz with a small driver: `kernel/driver.v1.md` defines its four commands, `adapters/template/` is a minimal one to copy, and a five-check test kit shows whether a driver passes.
Records v1 publishes the rules any tool follows to keep a project's work on GitHub, with a kit that reports each record breaking them.
The release package carries the three host drivers and the driver kit; the kit never copies a credential into its output, and the template driver leaves no agent running.
`install skills` no longer deletes a file of yours at its staging or backup path, and no longer refuses every agent when `~/.config` is a link.
`openwiz init` reports a label only when GitHub shows it, and an install made before the removals still passes `install status` and updates.
